title: Multiplication of a finite separable extension is etale
statement: Let $k'/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] which is finite ($\dim_kk'<\infty$) and separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $\mu:k'\otimes_kk'\to k'$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, be the multiplication map. Then $\operatorname{Spec}\mu:\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}(k'\otimes_kk')$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]; in particular $\mu$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QH (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-separable-algebraic, line 47219), proof, second paragraph: 'Since $k'/k$ is an etale extension of rings, we see that $k'\otimes_kk'\to k'$ is etale (Lemma 00U2)'. A route in Stacks: Lemma 0C2X (lemma-separable-algebraic-diagonal, line 10221) identifies $\mu$ with a localization $k'\otimes_kk'\to(k'\otimes_kk')_Q$ at one element ($k'=k(\alpha)$, $Q$ the cofactor of $x-\alpha$ in the minimal polynomial), etale by Lemma 00U2 (1) (lemma-etale, line 39290); etale implies smooth by definition of an etale ring map (Stacks 00U1).

proof.text: Since $k'/k$ is finite and separable algebraic, the morphism $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ induced by $k\to k'$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale].

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QH (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-separable-algebraic, line 47219), proof, second paragraph: 'Since $k'/k$ is an etale extension of rings'; that is Lemma Tag 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field, line 39394)

proof.text: Let $i_1:k'\to k'\otimes_kk'$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] with $R=k$, $A=k'$ (so that $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale by step 1) and $S=k'$, the morphism $g:=\operatorname{Spec}i_1:\operatorname{Spec}(k'\otimes_kk')\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$ is etale.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00U2 (lemma-etale, line 39290), part (3): a base change of an etale ring map is etale; this is the 'Lemma 00U2' cited in the proof of Lemma Tag 07QH

proof.text: The multiplication map satisfies $\mu\circ i_1=\mathrm{id}_{k'}$, since $\mu(a\otimes1)=a\cdot1=a$ for $a\in k'$. As $\operatorname{Spec}$ is a contravariant functor [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $f:=\operatorname{Spec}\mu:\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}(k'\otimes_kk')$ satisfies $g\circ f=\operatorname{Spec}(\mu\circ i_1)=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{id}_{k'})=\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}k'}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QH, proof, second paragraph (the factorization $k'\to A\otimes_kk'\to A$ with $A=k'$)

proof.text: The identity $\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}k'}$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] (an isomorphism onto the open subscheme $\operatorname{Spec}k'$ of itself), hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1). So in $\operatorname{Spec}k'\xrightarrow{f}\operatorname{Spec}(k'\otimes_kk')\xrightarrow{g}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ both $g\circ f$ (step 3) and $g$ (step 2) are etale, and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (3) gives that $f=\operatorname{Spec}\mu$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. (This is the scheme form of Algebra, Lemma 00U7: $\mu$ is a $k'$-algebra map between the etale $k'$-algebras $k'\otimes_kk'$ and $k'$.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale) and Lemma Tag 02GW (lemma-etale-permanence, line 8491); ring version Algebra, Lemma Tag 00U7 (lemma-map-between-etale, algebra.tex line 39508)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], since $\operatorname{Spec}\mu$ is etale, $\mu$ is an etale ring map: $k'$ is a finitely presented $(k'\otimes_kk')$-algebra, $H_1(L_{k'/k'\otimes_kk'})=0$ and $\Omega_{k'/k'\otimes_kk'}=0$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. The zero module is a finite projective $k'$-module (a direct summand of the finite free module $0$), so conditions (i), (ii), (iii) of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] hold and $\mu$ is a smooth ring map.

source.place: Definition Tag 00U1 (definition-etale): an etale ring map is a smooth ring map with $\Omega_{S/R}=0$

split_report.summary: Statement kept (it matches what the proof of Stacks 07QH uses: the multiplication map of a finite separable extension is etale, and smooth as an etale ring map). Stacks' proof of 07QH says only 'k'/k is etale, so k'(x)k' -> k' is etale (Lemma 00U2)'; the missing argument is written out along Stacks' own lemmas: k -> k' etale (00U3, new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale), base change k' -> k'(x)k' etale (00U2(3), existing leaf lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change), mu o i_1 = id, and cancellation (00U7 / Morphisms 02GW, existing leaf lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation) gives Spec mu etale; smoothness from the identification lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine (02GJ) and Definition 00U1 (Omega = 0 is finite projective). The route via the primitive element and Lemma 0C2X (localization at one element, 00U2(1)) suggested in source.place was not taken: it would need nodes for the primitive element theorem, the isomorphism k'[x]/(P) = k'(x)k' and the localization identification, none of which exist, while every piece of the chosen route is already a node (four of them Mathlib leaves). All tags checked against tags/tags: 07QH, 00U1, 00U2, 00U3, 00U7, 02GJ, 02GL, 02GP, 02GW, 0C2X; 00U8 is lemma-surjective-flat-finitely-presented and 02GE is morphisms-lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism, neither used.
